title: KnowledgeVIS: Interpreting Language Models by Comparing Fill-in-the-Blank Prompts
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical associations, moral qualities, and affiliations related to different religious groups by analyzing model predictions for fill-in-the-blank prompts.
findings: RoBERTa exhibited strong biases, associating Islam, Hinduism, and Christianity with marriage and morality (e.g., 'polygamy', 'patriarchy', 'evil'), in contrast to Judaism, Buddhism, and Sikhism which were associated with peace and service (e.g., 'tolerant', 'good'). RoBERTa also frequently suggested an association between Communism and 'Jewish'. In contrast, BERT showed very few negative associations with religion.
